title: Hip hop
description: Boom bap: the half-time kick, the drunken swing, the 808 sub and chopped piano, on the skills from the core lessons.
author: Strudel Workshop

tracks.title: Boom bap
tracks.blurb: Half-time drums, swung hats, an 808 sub and piano chops: a beat from the SP-1200 era.

lessons.title: Half-time
lessons.goal: Lay down the boom bap: kick on 1 and the "and" of 3, snare on 2 and 4, at 90 BPM.
lessons.concept:
Hip hop drums came from drum breaks chopped on an **SP-1200** or an **MPC**, and the pattern underneath most of them is **boom bap**: a kick (boom) on beat 1, a snare (bap) on 2 and 4, and a second kick pushed to the "and" of 3. At 90 BPM the groove feels **half-time**, like it’s leaning back.

Write the kick over 8ths: `"bd ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ bd ~"` is eight steps, so the second kick lands halfway through beat 4’s run-up, on the "and" of 3. The TR-808 gives the deep, round boom. There are no vocal samples here, so these beats stay instrumental.

tasks.text: A part called kick: TR-808, on beat 1 and the "and" of 3, written over 8ths.
tasks.hint: const kick = s("bd ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ bd ~").bank("RolandTR808"), then stack(kick).

tasks.text: A part called snare on beats 2 and 4, and stack it.

challenge.text: Add a second snare hit: a quiet one on the last 16th of the bar.

summary: Boom bap: kick on 1 and the "and" of 3, snare on 2 and 4.
Writing over 8ths ("bd ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ bd ~") places the second kick.

lessons.title: Swung hats
lessons.goal: Add 16th hats with a heavy swing and a gain pattern.
lessons.concept:
Swing is what separates a hip hop beat from a drum machine preset. The MPC’s swing setting pushed every second 16th late; **DJ Premier** kept it tight, **J Dilla** pushed it until the hats sounded drunk. Here `.swingBy(.2, 8)` is about 60% swing: lazy but still locked.

A **gain pattern** keeps the hats from sounding like a sewing machine: the hit on the beat loud, the ones between quiet. `"[.5 .25 .35 .25]*4"` lines up with `hh*16`, one value per hat.

tasks.text: A part called hats: 16th closed hats on the 808, with the hit on each beat loudest.
tasks.hint: const hats = s("hh*16").bank("RolandTR808").gain("[.5 .25 .35 .25]*4"), and stack it.

challenge.text: Open a hat on the "and" of 4, right before the bar turns around.
challenge.hint: const open = s("~ ~ ~ [~ oh]").bank("RolandTR808").gain(.4), and stack it.

summary: .swingBy(.2, 8) is about 60% swing: the Dilla lean.
A gain pattern on 16th hats puts the weight on the beat.
An open hat on the "and" of 4 marks the turnaround.

lessons.title: The 808 sub
lessons.goal: Put a long sine bass under the kick, in a key.
lessons.concept:
The **808 bass** is the kick drum’s long tail turned into a note: a pure sine, low, that rings out. In Strudel we build it from `s("sine")` with a slow `.release`, so each note hangs after it’s struck.

It plays on the kick’s rhythm, so the boom and the bass become one sound. `n("0 ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ 0 ~").scale("C1:minor")` picks scale degrees in the first octave: the 1 in the scale name is what makes it a sub. Keep it low in the mix: on laptop speakers you may barely hear it, but on anything with a woofer it’s the whole beat.

tasks.text: A part called sub: a sine playing scale degree 0 of C1 minor on the kick’s rhythm.
tasks.hint: const sub = n("0 ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ 0 ~").scale("C1:minor").s("sine"), and stack it.

tasks.text: Let it ring: a release of about half a second, and gain .8.

challenge.text: Move the second note to degree 2 (the flat third) so the bass walks.

summary: An 808 bass is a low sine with a long release.
scale("C1:minor"): the 1 puts the notes in the sub octave.
Play it on the kick’s rhythm so boom and bass are one sound.

lessons.title: Piano chops
lessons.goal: Chop a piano chord into a syncopated stab.
lessons.concept:
Boom bap was built on **chopped samples**: a bar of a soul record, cut into pieces on the SP-1200 and replayed off the pads. We have no records to chop, but the move translates: a sampled piano chord, cut short with `.clip`, placed on an off-grid rhythm with `.struct`.

`.struct("[~ x ~ ~] [~ ~ x ~] [~ x ~ ~] [~ ~ x ~]")` writes two hits per two beats, neither on the beat. `.clip(.4)` cuts each hit to 40% of its step, like lifting a finger off a pad. A little `.room` puts the piano on a dusty record instead of in the room with you.

tasks.text: A part called keys: a Cm7 piano chord struck on the 2nd 16th of beat 1 and the 3rd 16th of beat 2 (then again in beats 3 and 4).
tasks.hint: const keys = chord("Cm7").voicing().struct("[~ x ~ ~] [~ ~ x ~] [~ x ~ ~] [~ ~ x ~]").s("piano").gain(.5), and stack it.

tasks.text: Cut each hit short, like a pad release: clip .4.
Put it on a dusty record: a little reverb.

challenge.text: Alternate two chords across bars: Cm7, then Fm7.

summary: .struct places a chord off the grid, like pads on an SP-1200.
A touch of .room makes a piano sound sampled.

lessons.title: Ghost kicks and the drunken feel
lessons.goal: Add a quiet extra kick and swing the kick itself.
lessons.concept:
Listen to a Dilla beat and the kick never sits exactly where a drum machine would put it. Two things are going on: **ghost kicks**, quiet extra hits that fill the gaps, and **swing on the kick**, not only on the hats, so the whole kit leans together.

`"bd ~ ~ [~ bd] ~ ~ bd ~"` adds a kick on the last 16th of beat 2; a gain pattern with a `.3` in that slot makes it a ghost. Then `.swingBy(.2, 8)` on the kick line pushes it the same way as the hats. The snare stays straight: that’s the tension that makes it feel drunk rather than sloppy.

tasks.text: Add a ghost kick on the last 16th of beat 2, at gain .3.
Swing the kick like the hats.

challenge.text: Drop the first kick every fourth bar, so the loop breathes.
challenge.hint: Add .lastOf(4, x => x.mask("0 1 1 1 1 1 1 1")) to the kick line.

summary: Ghost kicks are quiet extra hits in the gaps.
Swinging the kick as well as the hats gives the drunken feel.
Keep the snare straight: the tension is the point.

lessons.title: Project: The beat
lessons.goal: Build a boom bap beat from scratch with one key for everything.
lessons.concept:
Everything from this pack in one loop: the half-time kick with a ghost, a straight snare, swung hats, the 808 sub and piano chops, all in one key. A `const key` at the top keeps the sub and the piano agreeing, and makes a different key a one-line change.

Aim for 88–95 BPM. Keep the piano and sub under the drums: the kick and snare are the record; everything else is the sample around them.

tasks.text: Add swung 16th hats with a gain pattern.
tasks.hint: const hats = s("hh*16").bank("RolandTR808").gain("[.5 .25 .35 .25]*4").swingBy(.2, 8), and stack it.

tasks.text: Add the 808 sub in the key, on the kick’s two main hits, ringing out.
Add piano chops in the key: a chord stab, clipped short, with a little room, under gain .6.
tasks.hint: const keys = chord("<Cm7 Fm7>").voicing().struct("[~ x ~ ~] [~ ~ x ~] [~ x ~ ~] [~ ~ x ~]").s("piano").clip(.4).room(.3).gain(.5)

challenge.text: Change the key to F minor: one edit, and both the sub and the piano follow.

summary: A boom bap beat: half-time kick with a ghost, straight snare, swung hats, 808 sub, piano chops.
One const key keeps the sub and the piano in tune.
Drums on top; the sample sits underneath.
